text.p: Monsanto Co. reported a 5 percent rise in first-quarter profits Tuesday, posting increases in sales from its agricultural and pharmaceutical units and declines in chemicals and food ingredients.
The St. Louis-based company had net income of $274 million, or 45 cents a share, compared with $260 million, or 43 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996.

The results included an after-tax charge of $63 million, or 10 cents a share, to write off research and development in connection with the acquisition of Asgrow Agronomics and a smaller seed company in Brazil.
"We're continuing to get strong performance from our business operations, allowing us to make substantial investments in growth," Chairman Robert Shapiro said.
"At the same time, we're positioning our life science and chemical businesses to get off to a strong start once the spinoff is complete," he added in a statement.
Monsanto previously said it would spin off its chemical operations.

The company said its agricultural products sales expanded to $1.07 billion from $825 million, although operating income fell to $224 million, after the research charge, from $272 million. Excluding the charge, the agricultural operating profit would have been a record, the company said.

Monsanto said its G.D. Searle pharmaceutical sales rose to $515 million from $477 million, but operating income fell to $55 million from $60 million. The year-ago quarter benefited from cost-sharing alliances, Monsanto said.
Sales of food ingredients such as Nutra-Sweet fell to $260 million from $266 million, but operating profit rose to $43 million from $25 million due to reduced costs.
Chemicals sales slipped to $732 million from $736 million while operating profit rose to $81 million from $64 million.
Monsanto's stock lost 25 cents to $39.25 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
